parts.label: (a)
parts.note: A = {3, 6, 9, 12, 15}, B = {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15} (30 itself is outside the universal set); A intersect B = {3, 6, 15}. Both agree.

parts.label: (b)
parts.note: A' intersect B' = (A union B)'; A union B has 9 elements, so 15 - 9 = 6, namely {4, 7, 8, 11, 13, 14}. Both give 6.

key_verdict: No disagreement; the setter's key is correct in both parts.
why: Exactly the shape of a real 2-mark P1 sets item: set-builder universal set, 'List the elements', 'Find n(...)', and (b) quietly tests De Morgan. The 2025 P2 Q7(a) exemplar shares only the generic factors/multiples setup; its task (agree/disagree with statements) is different, so this is not a re-skin.
